title: Researching Research for Ayurveda
subtitle: A Journey
description: A book reflecting Dr. Bhatt's journey through research for Ayurveda, structured to provide depth and clarity on fundamentals, inquiry, experimentation and solution identification.
long_description:
Ayurveda has never lacked for texts. What it has lacked is an account of how one actually researches it how a classical proposition becomes a question, how a question becomes an experiment, and how an experiment becomes something a regulator, a clinician or a manufacturer can act on.

This book is written from inside that problem. Across five decades spanning clinical practice, academic institutions, industrial R&D and formal research, Dr. Bhatt sets out the reasoning that has to happen before a study is designed at all: which parts of the classical corpus carry reproducible signal, which questions are worth the cost of answering, and where enthusiasm for Ayurveda has repeatedly outrun its evidence.

It is organised as a journey rather than a manual, moving from fundamentals through inquiry and experimentation to the identification of workable solutions. Readers who want to understand why so much Ayurveda research produces so little translatable outcome will find the argument laid out plainly.
highlights: Written from five decades across clinic, academia, industry and research
Moves from fundamentals through inquiry and experimentation to solutions
Treats methodology as the subject, not an appendix to it
For researchers, postgraduate scholars and R&D teams in Ayurveda

title: Integrative Perspectives
subtitle: Ayurveda, Phytopharmaceuticals and Natural Products
description: A landmark publication by IASTAM in association with Continental Prakashan, Pune, comprising 51 chapters by 41 well-known experts and IASTAM awardees; it explains integration in Ayurveda, especially drug standardization and regulatory aspects.
long_description:
Integration is the word everyone in Ayurveda uses and few define. This volume is an attempt at the definition assembled not as a single argument but as 51 chapters from 41 contributors, each an established expert or IASTAM awardee writing from their own domain.

The centre of gravity is drug standardization and the regulatory apparatus around it: the part of the field where claims either survive contact with analytical method and law, or quietly do not. Around that centre the contributors work through phytopharmaceuticals, natural products, pharmaceutics and the points where classical preparation and modern analytics genuinely meet rather than merely coexist.

Published by IASTAM in association with Continental Prakashan, Pune, it is a reference volume rather than a monograph intended to sit on the desk of anyone working on the standardization, regulation or industrial development of Ayurvedic and natural products.
highlights: 51 chapters by 41 experts and IASTAM awardees
Centred on drug standardization and regulatory aspects
Covers phytopharmaceuticals, natural products and pharmaceutics
Published by IASTAM with Continental Prakashan, Pune
